correctness.rationale: Henson universal homogeneous K_{r+1}-free graph has quantifier elimination, so each complete ordered distinct pair type over named P corresponds uniquely to a finite allowed adjacency diagram. Unary neighborhoods must miss a part, giving U. For nonadjacent x,y there are U^2 choices. For adjacent x,y the only forbidden new K_{r+1} has r-1 common neighboring parameters; unary admissibility then forces a unique omitted part on which both neighborhoods are empty. For each other part, 4^{n_j}-3^{n_j} joint adjacency assignments have nonempty intersection, and cases for omitted i are disjoint, giving correction B. For fixed r and all parts growing, binomial product expansions give B/U^2=beta+O_r(s+(3/4)^{n_min}), the stated collision law; Cauchy and integrality prove sharpness. An independent exhaustive generator checked 41 small configurations including r=4. The proof, not finite experiments, establishes infinity-wide scope.

value.rationale: Complete r-partite named parameter graphs at clique size r are the natural maximal clique-width boundary of Henson H_{r+1}. The result gives a full exact adjacent/nonadjacent two-type census for every r>=4 and every positive part-size vector, identifies the unique-bad-part obstruction, and exhibits a sharp universal collision-entropy asymptotic distinguishing balanced and strongly imbalanced diagrams. The limit (r-1)/(2r-1) and its eventually-balanced equality criterion are motivated consequences with mathematical content beyond recomputing an existing table.
